title: C. elegans Worm Size Measurement Protocol
author: Laura Breimann
materials: Save images for one condition in a folder.
Grow worms to the desired stage.

steps.title: Synchronize worms to desired stage
steps.instruction: Choose a synchronization method (picking, bleaching, or hand selection). For the picking method, pick at least 20 gravid adult worms onto a fresh OP50 plate, allow them to lay eggs for 4 hours, then remove the adults; keep worm number and egg‑laying time constant across plates.

substeps.instruction: Pick ≥20 gravid adults onto fresh OP50 plate.
Remove adults; maintain consistent numbers and timing.

steps.title: Wash worms with M9 buffer
steps.instruction: Wash worms off the plate using M9 buffer. Let worms settle in a tube for 10 minutes, carefully replace the M9 with fresh M9, and repeat this wash three times. After the final wash, remove most of the liquid leaving approximately 20 µL with the worms.

substeps.instruction: Replace M9 with fresh M9 (1st wash).
Repeat replacement two more times (total 3 washes).
Leave ~20 µL of M9 with worms.

steps.title: Anesthetize worms and transfer to agar
steps.instruction: Add 10 mM Levamisole to the worm suspension, wait 5 minutes, then gently pipette the worms onto an unseeded agar plate, keeping the liquid volume minimal to avoid interference with later image analysis.

steps.title: Spread worms evenly on plate
steps.instruction: Using an eyelash pick, separate the worms so they are evenly spaced, not touching each other or the plate edge. Optionally mark the plate bottom with thin lines to aid orientation during imaging.

steps.title: Capture calibrated images of worms
steps.instruction: Place a microscope calibration ruler on the same slide, keep camera zoom and microscope settings constant for the whole experiment, and acquire images with an eyepiece camera (e.g., Dino‑Eye AM4025X) or a phone adapter. Save raw files if the camera supports them; otherwise use the available format. Avoid imaging the same worm twice.

substeps.instruction: Capture images with Dino‑Eye AM4025X or phone adapter.

steps.title: Install WormSizer plugin in Fiji
steps.instruction: Open Fiji, go to Help → Update → Manage Update Sites, check “WormSizer”, click Close and Apply changes, then restart Fiji. The WormSizer plugin will appear in the Plugins menu.

steps.title: Set input folders and calibration length
steps.instruction: In WormSizer, select the input directory containing the worm images and an output directory for results, then click the “>>” button. Next, set the length in microns that corresponds to the calibration ruler (e.g., 1000 µm for a 1 mm segment).

substeps.instruction: Enter ruler length in microns (e.g., 1000 µm).

steps.title: Run WormSizer detection on images
steps.instruction: Adjust outline‑detection settings appropriate for the magnification, then press the “>>” button to start detection across all images. Wait for the processing‑complete image that signals detection has finished.

steps.title: Review and curate worm detections
steps.instruction: Open the output folder, load the experiment .xml file, and use the magnifying symbol to step through each detected worm. Mark each worm as TRUE (include) or FALSE (exclude); the results .csv file updates the “pass” column in real time. The plugin generates three files: a settings .csv, an experiment .xml, and a results .csv.

substeps.instruction: Set pass = TRUE/FALSE for each worm.
Note generated files: settings .csv, experiment .xml, results .csv.

steps.title: Compute microns‑per‑pixel resolution
steps.instruction: Open the calibration ruler image in Fiji, draw a line between two known points on the ruler (e.g., a 1 mm segment), press Command + M to obtain the pixel length, then calculate microns per pixel = 1000 µm ÷ pixel length. Record this value for downstream analysis; optional Python script for plotting is available in the referenced GitHub repository.

substeps.instruction: Draw line over known distance (1 mm).
Press Command + M to get pixel length.

description: Use Fiji to open the images and remove background. FIJI (FIJI Is Just ImageJ) Open image using Fiji Set the image to 8-bit: Image > Type > 8-bit Subtract background: Process -> Subtract Background. Set the preview checkbox to see how changing rolling ball radius changes the results. 4. Threshold: Image -> Adjust -> Threshold; where it says “Default”, change it to “Otsu”. Move the sliding bars so that you get as much of the worms highlighted, and as little of the background. Then click “Apply”. 5. Save the image to a new folder for further analysis.
